articles.title: AI Agent Development Cost in 2026: Real Price Ranges, Running Costs and How to Budget
articles.excerpt: I run a small AI agent team and get asked "how much will this cost?" every week, so I put the real 2026 numbers in one place. This was first published on the RixDigi blog. Short answer: a simple AI ag…
articles.body: I run a small AI agent team and get asked "how much will this cost?" every week, so I put the real 2026 numbers in one place. This was first published on the RixDigi blog . Short answer: a simple AI agent that handles one task costs about $15,000–$40,000 from a US or Western European agency and roughly $4,000–$20,000 from an offshore team. Agents that connect to several systems, such as a customer support or voice agent, usually cost $40,000–$150,000 in the US, or about a quarter to a half of that offshore. Running it adds about $150–$600 a month for model usage and hosting at small-business volumes, plus support. This guide shows where those numbers come from and how to keep yours at the low end.
articles.author: Aqib Rehman

articles.title: How Real-Time Dubbing Stays in Sync With a YouTube Video: Fitting Translated Speech Into Fixed Time Slots
articles.excerpt: I work on EarDub, a YouTube dubbing extension. The code is a teaching version written for this post, not EarDub's source. The table below is the planner's real output; the player sync function was onl…
articles.body: I work on EarDub, a YouTube dubbing extension. The code is a teaching version written for this post, not EarDub's source. The table below is the planner's real output; the player sync function was only tested against a mock player, so try it in your target browsers. This post was drafted with AI. A dubbed sentence has to start when the speaker starts and, ideally, end before the next sentence begins. The translation rarely cooperates. Keeping a dub in sync therefore comes down to three decisions per sentence: how much silence you can borrow, how far you can speed the voice up, and what to do when neither is enough. The problem has a name Dubbing researchers call it isochrony: the translated speech should occupy the same time as the original.

articles.title: PHP Module Boundaries: Why Folders and Dependency Declarations Are Not Enough
articles.excerpt: Coretsia Engineering Notes — 02 In the first Engineering Note, I explored an important distinction: a deterministic dependency order can still be incorrect. A similar distinction exists in modular arc…
articles.body: Coretsia Engineering Notes — 02 In the first Engineering Note , I explored an important distinction: a deterministic dependency order can still be incorrect. A similar distinction exists in modular architecture. A project can have well-organized directories, separate Composer packages, and explicit dependency declarations. Its code can pass functional tests, yet one package may still reach into another package's internals or depend on a package it never declared. The question is not merely whether the application runs, but whether the relationships between its components are the ones the architecture intended. This article demonstrates that distinction with a small PHP 8.4 experiment. No particular application framework is required. 1.
articles.author: Vladyslav

articles.title: Should background jobs call your own API over HTTP, or go straight to the database? Let's argue about it
articles.excerpt: Reliable HTTP cron and delayed-job scheduling with automatic retries and full run logs — delay.run Every background job eventually has to change something: mark invoices as overdue, expire trials, rec…
articles.body: Reliable HTTP cron and delayed-job scheduling with automatic retries and full run logs — delay.run Every background job eventually has to change something: mark invoices as overdue, expire trials, recalculate a leaderboard, send reminders. There are two ways to do it. Option A: the job connects to the database and runs the queries itself, using the same models or a few lines of SQL. Option B: the job calls your own application over HTTP ( POST /internal/invoices/mark-overdue ), and the application does the work, through the same code paths as any other request. Both are common. Teams switch from one to the other after an incident, and then sometimes switch back after a different incident. Let's argue about it. The case for going straight to the database It's simple and fast.

articles.body: Translation vendors hand you back a pile of translated strings. Your CI pipeline doesn't know or care whether those strings break your layout, mangle your plural logic, or silently drop a variable. That gap is exactly where most localisation bugs slip into production. There's a good breakdown of the linguistic vs. functional split in localisation testing over on M21Global's blog . This article picks up the other half: what you, as a developer, can actually automate and test in CI before a human ever opens the app.

articles.title: Moving cron jobs to a new server? A 12-point checklist so nothing runs twice, and nothing stops running
articles.excerpt: Reliable HTTP cron and delayed-job scheduling with automatic retries and full run logs — delay.run Migrating to a new server is mostly about the application, the database and DNS. Scheduled jobs are a…
articles.body: Reliable HTTP cron and delayed-job scheduling with automatic retries and full run logs — delay.run Migrating to a new server is mostly about the application, the database and DNS. Scheduled jobs are an afterthought. Someone runs crontab -l > crontab.txt on the old box near the end, pastes it on the new one, and the migration is declared done. Then the problems show up over the following weeks. The nightly invoice job runs on both servers and every customer gets two emails. The backup job is still running on the old server, which is about to be deleted, and backing up a database nobody uses anymore. The cleanup job that was in /etc/cron.d/ never moved at all. Here's the checklist. Inventory 1. Find every place schedules live, not just your crontab.

Previously paired scales will continue syncing, but disconnecting them could mean losing automatic weight tracking for good. Smart home gadgets have a habit of outliving the software that makes them smart. A device can work perfectly well for years, only to lose some of its most useful features when its manufacturer decides it’s time to move on. articles.title: SpaceX launches 2 rockets from same pad 32 hours apart, smashing turnaround record (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX just launched two rockets from the same California pad 32 hours apart, breaking its own turnaround record by about 13 hours.
articles.body: SpaceX set a new record with its latest satellite launch out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base 's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov. 22) at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California), on a mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) called NROL-136. It was the second launch from that pad in a little over 32 hours, after the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force . And that quick turnaround made history. Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn!
